-72.99700,41.25380.name: Yale Fertility Center
-72.99700,41.25380.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Emre Seli, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-9.14918,38.72847.name: Ava Clinic
-9.14918,38.72847.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

127.11837,37.32777.name: Nonclinical Research Institute
127.11837,37.32777.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of CORESTEMCHEMON Inc.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-79.49963,43.77412.name: York University
-79.49963,43.77412.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, May 2026
-79.49963,43.77412.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, May 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-43.31000,-22.73500.name: Pan American Foot and Mouth Disease Center (PANAFTOSA)
-43.31000,-22.73500.state: Cidade Administrativa do Governo de, Prédio Gerais Rod. Papa João Paul, Brazil
-43.31000,-22.73500.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, planned. Run by The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO). It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. Operational or announced: Announced 2021. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-46.68700,-23.59000.name: Suzano / FuturaGene
-46.68700,-23.59000.state: São Paulo — Av. Brigadeiro Faria Lima 1355
-46.68700,-23.59000.desc: The world’s largest pulp producer, growing engineered eucalyptus approved in Brazil for commercial planting. It is the first engineered forest tree commercialised anywhere, on plantations measured in millions of hectares. Trees are not annual crops: they flower for decades, spread pollen for kilometres, and outlast every company and regulator involved in approving them.

-118.44300,34.04300.name: California Cryobank / Generate Life Sciences
-118.44300,34.04300.desc: One of the largest sperm banks in the world, with published family limits that cap how many families may use one donor. The limits are voluntary, self-enforced, count families rather than children, and nothing counts across banks or borders — which is why donor-conceived people keep finding sibling groups far larger than any published cap implies.

104.87000,11.53000.name: Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute
104.87000,11.53000.desc: Holds Cambodia’s rice collections, including traditional varieties from a country whose agricultural knowledge was deliberately destroyed in the 1970s. Rebuilding a seed system after that is a different problem from developing one, and the collections are what made it possible at all.
